info.text:
Every car lease is secretly a bet on a used car.

Example: a $40,000 car, 36 months, 58% residual. The lessor bets it's worth $23,200 later; you pay the $16,800 drop (about $467/month) plus a money factor (about 6% APR here, $158/month).
In Q2 2008, falling truck and SUV values cost Ford Credit a $2.1B lease charge.
Moody's: about 75% of leased cars usually come back; by mid-2022, about 10% did, as many drivers bought at the preset price.
GM Financial's leased cars carried $25.0B in estimated residual value at the end of 2025; its 10-K says a 1% drop in residuals would add about $250M in depreciation.

Sources: Ford Credit 2008 filings, GM FY2025 10-K, Moody's Analytics (2023).
News and education, not financial advice.
